samples.summary: New list commands on NoteEditorAPI mutate the document with no read-only/editable guard, unlike the checkbox input handler added in the same change
samples.evidence: `editor.ts:524-528` wires `toggleBulletList/​toggleOrderedList/​toggleTaskList/​indentList/​outdentList` straight to `list-commands.ts`, which dispatch `view.dispatch(...)` unconditionally (`list-commands.ts` `replacePrefixes`). Nothing in `list-commands.ts` checks `state.readOnly` or the `EditorView.editable` facet, even though `checkbox-input.ts:24-29` added exactly that two-way guard for the same mount modes and `docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-list-controls-lessons.md:20` states a note can be non-writable two ways. The only current caller gates on UI state (`notes-toolbar.tsx:241` `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"`), so the protection lives in the frontend, not in the engine. Any consumer holding the `NoteEditorAPI` from a read-only mount (`NotesView` exposes it via `onEditorReady`, `notes-view.tsx:119`) reaches the mutation. Note the pre-existing `toggleBold`/`insertTable` have the same gap, so this may be an accepted pattern; the fix belongs in `list-commands.ts`/`editor.ts`.

samples.summary: Dropping `label: true` from markdown-it-task-lists changes the rendered HTML for every preview, including read-only share-link previews that gain nothing from the change
samples.evidence: `preview.ts:53` changes `md.use(taskLists, { label: true, enabled: false })` to `{ enabled: true }`. `md` is a module-level singleton shared by every `NotePreview`, including the read-only mount used by the viewer share link (`packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:345` → `notes-view.tsx:110` with `readOnly`), where no click handler is attached at all. Those previews lose the `<label>` that associated the checkbox with its item text (an assistive-tech association, not just a click target) while getting no interactivity in return. I found no CSS keyed on the label (`packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-preview.css` has no `label`/`task` rules besides the new ones), so this is an a11y/markup regression rather than a layout break.

samples.summary: computeActiveFormats now walks every selected line on every doc/selection change, a per-keystroke O(selection) cost on an existing hot subscription
samples.evidence: `editor.ts:383-388` calls `computeActiveFormats(u.state)` on every `docChanged || selectionSet` update, and `commands.ts:65` now adds `computeListState(state)`, which `selectedLines()` (`list-commands.ts`) materialises as a parsed object per selected line plus a regex per line. Previously the function was O(1) around the caret. With a select-all in a large note the toolbar subscription (`notes-toolbar.tsx:232-237`, plus a React setState per update) re-parses the whole document on every keystroke. The callers were not changed to debounce or bail out for large selections.

samples.summary: Tab (`indentWithTab`) and vim's own indent still indent list lines with CodeMirror's generic indent unit, which disagrees with the new list indent model the toolbar enforces
samples.evidence: `editor.ts:335,338` bind `indentWithTab` in both keymaps; it indents by the CodeMirror indent unit regardless of list structure. The new `indentList` (`list-commands.ts` `indentStep`) refuses to indent when there is no sibling above and uses the parent's content column (three columns after `1. `). So Tab produces indentation the toolbar reports as impossible (`formats.canIndent === false` while Tab happily indents) and at a width that can differ from what `indentList` would have produced, giving two inconsistent indent behaviours over the same markdown. `docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-list-controls-todo.md:61` records the no-rebind choice as a deliberate non-goal, so this may be accepted scope.

samples.summary: packages/notes README's "Public API" list is stale: the newly exported `NoteListKind` is not listed
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/index.ts:22` adds `export type { NoteListKind } from './view/list-commands.js';` but `packages/notes/README.md:34-38`, which enumerates the exports of `src/index.ts`, still lists only `NoteInlineFormats` alongside the view exports.

finding.summary: New list commands on NoteEditorAPI mutate the document with no read-only/editable guard, unlike the checkbox input handler added in the same change
finding.evidence: `editor.ts:524-528` wires `toggleBulletList/​toggleOrderedList/​toggleTaskList/​indentList/​outdentList` straight to `list-commands.ts`, which dispatch `view.dispatch(...)` unconditionally (`list-commands.ts` `replacePrefixes`). Nothing in `list-commands.ts` checks `state.readOnly` or the `EditorView.editable` facet, even though `checkbox-input.ts:24-29` added exactly that two-way guard for the same mount modes and `docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-list-controls-lessons.md:20` states a note can be non-writable two ways. The only current caller gates on UI state (`notes-toolbar.tsx:241` `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"`), so the protection lives in the frontend, not in the engine. Any consumer holding the `NoteEditorAPI` from a read-only mount (`NotesView` exposes it via `onEditorReady`, `notes-view.tsx:119`) reaches the mutation. verdict.reason: The code is present as described (list-commands.ts:193-211 dispatches unconditionally; editor.ts:527-531 exposes it), but the finding's bypass path does not exist in this repo. Only two NotesView mount sites exist. The single read-only mount, shared-document.tsx:345, passes no onEditorReady and renders no toolbar (shared-document.tsx:333-346), so no consumer ever holds a NoteEditorAPI from a read-only mount — notes-view.tsx:119 is an optional callback that is undefined there. The only mount that does hand out the API, notes-detail.tsx:196-201, passes no readOnly (writable), and its sole consumer of the five list methods (notes-toolbar.tsx:292-320) is inside the `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"` gate (notes-toolbar.tsx:241,246). Inside the engine, the read-only mount already removes every other mutation entry point: preview task toggle omitted (editor.ts:230-232), no history keymap (editor.ts:300), no image upload (editor.ts:212,391), and EditorView.editable.of(!readOnly) (editor.ts:376). No reachable path reaches the list mutations on a read-only note, so this is not a guard with a reachable bypass under the blast-radius rubric; what is left is a defense-in-depth observation statable entirely from the diff (checkbox-input.ts vs list-commands.ts), which the finding itself notes is the pre-existing pattern for toggleBold/insertTable.
